raw_evidence_cards.document_title: AGL: a Scalable System for Industrial-purpose Graph Machine Learning
raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: AGL is a scalable, fault-tolerant, integrated system for industrial-purpose graph machine learning that enables GNN training and inference on graphs with billions of nodes and hundred billions of edges using MapReduce and parameter servers.
overlaps: Distributed training framework for large-scale graphs via MapReduce and parameter servers
Fast model training on graphs with billions of nodes and edges
differences: Does not use graph summarization to compress graph data
Does not incorporate a temporal learning module for dynamic graphs
Focuses on static graphs rather than dynamic/evolving graphs

sources.title: AGL: a Scalable System for Industrial-purpose Graph Machine Learning
sources.quote: In this paper, we design AGL, a scalable, fault-tolerance and integrated system, with fully-functional training and inference for GNNs. Our system design follows the message passing scheme underlying the computations of GNNs. We design to generate the $k$-hop neighborhood, an information-complete subgraph for each node, as well as do the inference simply by merging values from in-edge neighbors and propagating values to out-edge neighbors via MapReduce.

sources.title: AGL: a Scalable System for Industrial-purpose Graph Machine Learning
sources.quote: Our system AGL, implemented on mature infrastructures, can finish the training of a 2-layer graph attention network on a graph with billions of nodes and hundred billions of edges in 14 hours, and complete the inference in 1.2 hour.

raw_evidence_cards.document_title: Temporal Graph Networks for Deep Learning on Dynamic Graphs
raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: Temporal Graph Networks (TGNs) is a generic, efficient framework for deep learning on dynamic graphs represented as sequences of timed events, combining memory modules and graph-based operators for temporal representation learning.
overlaps: Temporal learning module for dynamic graphs (sequence of timed events)
Efficient representation learning on dynamic graphs
differences: Does not use graph summarization to compress graph data
Does not incorporate a distributed training framework
Focuses on model architecture rather than system-level optimization for large-scale graphs

sources.title: Temporal Graph Networks for Deep Learning on Dynamic Graphs
sources.quote: In this paper, we present Temporal Graph Networks (TGNs), a generic, efficient framework for deep learning on dynamic graphs represented as sequences of timed events. Thanks to a novel combination of memory modules and graph-based operators, TGNs are able to significantly outperform previous approaches being at the same time more computationally efficient.

raw_evidence_cards.document_title: AliGraph: A Comprehensive Graph Neural Network Platform
raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: AliGraph is a comprehensive graph neural network platform consisting of distributed graph storage, optimized sampling operators and runtime to efficiently support GNN training on large-scale graphs.
overlaps: Distributed graph storage and runtime for large-scale GNN training
Efficient training on graphs with billions of vertices and edges
differences: Does not use graph summarization to compress graph data
Does not incorporate a temporal learning module for dynamic graphs
Focuses on static graph scenarios rather than dynamic/evolving graphs

sources.title: AliGraph: A Comprehensive Graph Neural Network Platform
sources.quote: In this paper, we present a comprehensive graph neural network system, namely AliGraph, which consists of distributed graph storage, optimized sampling operators and runtime to efficiently support not only existing popular GNNs but also a series of in-house developed ones for different scenarios.
